title: "Conclusion & Practical Validation of the MLOps Guidelines"

As part of the AIML4OS project, a two-day in-person workshop was held in Wiesbaden, Germany, on 15–16 October 2026, bringing together representatives from 10 participating National Statistical Institutes (NSIs) and Eurostat.

The workshop was organized within Work Package 10, From Text to Code, and provided an opportunity for the different clusters to share their progress, present methodological results, demonstrate their developed solutions and exchange experiences.

Within this broader workshop, Cluster 4 organized a dedicated subgroup activity to test the proposed MLOps Guidelines against concrete Machine Learning use cases. The objective was to assess their clarity, relevance, and practical applicability, while collecting feedback from participants to identify potential gaps, challenges, and opportunities for improvement.

This activity also provided an opportunity to exchange experiences across countries and better understand the different approaches and maturity levels regarding MLOps practices

# Workshop Organization and Methodology

The activity was organized into four subgroups, each supported by a Cluster 4 member. Participants had approximately 1.5 hours to work collaboratively on the assessment of a concrete ML use case using the proposed MLOps Guidelines.

Each group was asked to:

- Select a concrete use case representing an existing or ongoing Machine Learning project.

- Assess the use case against the MLOps Guidelines, using the proposed checklists to evaluate which practices were already implemented and identify areas for improvement.

- Identify gaps and challenges, both in the implementation of MLOps practices and in the applicability of the guidelines themselves.

- Provide feedback on the guidelines, highlighting unclear requirements, missing aspects, or potential improvements.

The exercise served a dual purpose: evaluating existing MLOps practices across different use cases and validating the guidelines themselves as a practical tool for supporting continuous improvement.

# Use Cases Evaluated

- **Use Case 1 – French ISCO at INSEE:** This use case focuses on the classification of occupations using the French national adaptation of ISCO. It involves collaboration between several units at INSEE (Census, Employment, and Household Surveys) and ministerial statistical services. The classification is applied to data from census, employment, and household surveys, which share similar questions and features.

# Key Learnings and Takeaways

The workshop provided valuable feedback on both the proposed guidelines and the current state of MLOps practices across the different use cases.

1. The checklists proved to be practical and easy to use

The participants were able to understand and apply the checklists without major difficulties. They provided a simple and structured way to assess an ML pipeline, quickly identify practices already in place, and highlight potential areas for improvement.

This confirmed the value of the checklists as a practical tool for evaluating MLOps maturity and guiding discussions within project teams.

2. MLOps maturity varies across teams and countries

The assessments highlighted different levels of MLOps maturity across the use cases and participating countries. This is a natural observation, as teams have different levels of experience, resources, project histories, and operational needs.

These differences reinforce the importance of having common guidelines that provide a shared reference while remaining flexible enough to accommodate different starting points.

3. Monitoring remains a common area for improvement

Across all four use cases, Part 4 of the guidelines, dedicated to monitoring, emerged as an area with significant potential for improvement.

While several MLOps practices are already in place, establishing systematic monitoring of models and pipelines remains a challenge. This highlights monitoring as an important area of focus for strengthening the reliability and long-term maintainability of ML solutions.

4. The guidelines should support continuous improvement, not act as rigid requirements

One of the key conclusions of the workshop was that the MLOps Guidelines should be understood as a framework for continuous improvement rather than a mandatory checklist that must be fully completed before deploying a model into production.

In practice, not every recommendation can or needs to be implemented from the beginning. Requiring full adherence to every guideline before deployment could unnecessarily slow down projects and prevent teams from delivering value.

Instead, the guidelines should help teams identify priorities, make informed decisions, and progressively improve their MLOps practices as their solutions evolve.

The ultimate objective is to develop ML pipelines that are more robust, maintainable, and adaptable, enabling teams to respond more efficiently to new data, changing requirements, and emerging challenges.

# Conclusion

The workshop confirmed that the MLOps Guidelines provide a useful and accessible framework for assessing existing ML pipelines and identifying improvement opportunities.

Rather than defining a fixed level of compliance, they establish a common direction for progressively strengthening MLOps practices across teams, while recognizing that different use cases may require different levels of implementation and maturity.
